subject: CloudHarbor security sprint sync — SSO, SCIM, IP allowlists & service-account plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: CloudHarbor security sprint sync — SSO, SCIM, IP allowlists & service-account plan

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, I wanted to capture a short plan for the security-focused implementation sprint and confirm owners and deliverables before we run the staging cutover. Proposed scope for this sprint:

- SAML SSO: finalize IdP metadata exchange, ACS/Entity IDs, and SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated behavior.
- SCIM: verify schema compatibility (user/group provisioning) and test provisioning loops.
- IP allowlists: provide staging and prod CIDR ranges; confirm egress/inbound rules for token/API traffic.
- Service accounts: agreement on ephemeral vs long-lived service accounts, naming pattern, and least-privilege roles.
- Org policies: any IAM org-level constraints (e.g., enforced 2FA, SCIM sync cadence) that will affect provisioning.

Proposed cutover window (staging dry run): 2026-10-02 01:00–05:00 UTC. Production cutover to follow after signoff (target week of 2026-10-11). Please let us know if those windows conflict with CloudHarbor maintenance.

Next steps / owners:
- CloudHarbor: confirm staging CIDRs + send completed security questionnaire (Aisha).
- Redwood: provide SAML metadata bundle and test user seed (Ben).
- Implementation: Monica will lead the SCIM runbook and test plans; Priyom will own service-account patterns.

I attached the short security questionnaire from our side — answering the SCIM schema and IP questions first will help reduce back-and-forth.

Thanks — look forward to the sync.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0129

Attachment: CloudHarbor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@cloudharbor.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Liu <david.liu@cloudharbor.com>, IT Ops <it@cloudharbor.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 11:43:00 -0400
Subject: Re: CloudHarbor security sprint sync — SSO, SCIM, IP allowlists & service-account plan

Ben —

Thanks for the write-up and the questionnaire. Quick answers up-front while we gather the attachments: the proposed staging window (2026-10-02) works for our ops team; production week for us looks fine too.

I've attached our completed questionnaire and a draft SCIM schema that our identity team uses (scim-schema-v2.json). A few clarifying items from our side:

1) SSO: We provision our IdP via Okta. We'll share the org-level metadata and want SP-initiated flows for application-initiated auth (most of our SSO is app-initiated). We do enforce signed assertions.

2) SCIM: We currently sync users and groups daily; during cutover we'd like to test an ad-hoc sync to validate mapping. Our schema includes a custom attribute (department_code) that we will need mapped.

3) IP allowlists: Staging CIDRs below. NOTE: outbound NAT will come from those ranges; you should allow inbound callbacks from 35.186.0.0/17 and 34.120.0.0/14 (these are our staging egress).
- staging: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24
- production: will provide after we finalize firewall planning (ETA 2026-09-14).

4) Service accounts: we prefer short-lived tokens with a rotation of 24 hours where possible. For any long-lived credentials we will require Host-based measurements (TOTP or hardware key) and a documented justification.

We attached the completed questionnaire and scim-schema-v2.json. I'll ask David to confirm the production egress ranges in a follow-up.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Bryant
Senior Security Program Manager | CloudHarbor
aisha.bryant@cloudharbor.com

Attachments: CloudHarbor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf); scim-schema-v2.json (application/json)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@cloudharbor.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudHarbor security sprint sync — SSO, SCIM, IP allowlists & service-account plan

Hi Aisha / Ben —

Thanks for the questionnaire and the SCIM schema — helpful detail. I'm attaching a short SCIM runbook draft in the Drive link Ben posted; highlights and clarifications below so we can lock the test cases before the staging dry run:

- Test users: we'll seed 3 test users with varying department_code values and 2 groups (engineering + ops).
- Provisioning cadence: we'll run an ad-hoc full sync during the staging window and validate create/update/delete behavior.
- Conflict handling: Redwood will treat CloudHarbor as the source of truth for SCIM attributes; we'll surface mismatches as warnings in the audit logs.
- Mapping for department_code: propose mapping to attribute 'urn:cloudharbor:departmentCode' on our side — Priyom, can you confirm we can accept a custom attribute?

Service-account notes:
- For tasks that require long-lived credentials (e.g., on-prem connectors), propose a named long-lived service account pattern: cloudharbor-int-<env>-<purpose>-svc (e.g., cloudharbor-int-staging-scim-svc). Long-lived accounts will have privileged roles scoped to narrow resources.
- For API-to-API calls we will use ephemeral tokens minted by our internal token service with 24-hour TTL by default.

If that all sounds good I'll convert the runbook into explicit test cases and a failure roll-back checklist.

—
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_confidential_playbook
From: David Liu <david.liu@cloudharbor.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@cloudharbor.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudHarbor security sprint sync — SSO, SCIM, IP allowlists & service-account plan

Monica / Ben —

Confirming production egress ranges: 34.120.0.0/14, 35.186.0.0/17, and 52.58.128.0/18. We validated the staging ranges Aisha listed.

On the custom SCIM attribute (department_code): we can expose it under the extension urn:cloudharbor:departmentCode — our team will include mapping instructions in the Drive doc by Monday.

Service accounts: agreed on the naming convention Monica suggested. For long-lived credentials we will submit a ticket to our security council with justification; the earliest they will approve such exceptions is Tue 2026-10-05, so if you need long-lived creds for the staging dry run please flag an exception request and we can expedite.

Finally, curious if Redwood can support a pre-cutover smoke test callback endpoint that returns a signed JWT for us to verify the SAML assertion flow end-to-end. If that's possible please advise the endpoint and sample request format.

Thanks — we'll aim to provide the production CIDRs and the updated mapping doc by 2026-09-14.

-David
David Liu
Cloud Infrastructure Lead | CloudHarbor
david.liu@cloudharbor.com
